title: Personnel Administration
topics: Human resource planning and job analysis
Nature and scope of personnel administration
Public service ethics, records and reform
The personnel office and its organisation

items.q: Personnel policy may be defined as
o: the standing statement of how an organisation intends to treat its people on hiring, pay and advancement
negotiation between representatives of workers and of the employer over the terms of employment
the systematic study of what a post involves in order to describe it and state what filling it demands
the longer preparation of a person for wider responsibilities rather than for the present post alone
items.s: Personnel policy: the standing statement of how an organisation intends to treat its people on hiring, pay and advancement. The other options describe Job analysis, Collective bargaining, Development.
items.t: The personnel office and its organisation

items.q: Which term is described by “an institution maintained to give serving officials instruction in administration and policy”?
o: Off the job training
On the job training
Mentoring
Staff college
items.s: Staff college is an institution maintained to give serving officials instruction in administration and policy.

items.q: Mentoring may be defined as
o: the strategic handling of people as an asset rather than merely as a cost to be controlled
instruction given at entry so that a new person learns the rules, routines and expectations of the organisation
a relationship in which a more experienced person guides the progress of a junior over time
a standard task or examination administered to applicants so that their abilities may be compared
items.s: Mentoring: a relationship in which a more experienced person guides the progress of a junior over time. The other options describe Human resource management, Selection test, Induction training.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Morale.
o: the periodic small addition to pay within a grade, granted for service or satisfactory conduct
a standard task or examination administered to applicants so that their abilities may be compared
the general confidence and willingness to cooperate that a group of workers displays
the approved list of posts, with their grades and numbers, that an organisation is authorised to maintain
items.s: Morale: the general confidence and willingness to cooperate that a group of workers displays. The other options describe Incremental step, Staff establishment, Selection test.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Staff turnover?
o: the rate at which people leave an organisation and are replaced
the statement of the standards of honesty and impartiality expected of those holding public office
a complaint by a serving person that they have been treated unfairly in a matter affecting their work
the assignment of available staff to the places where their services are most needed
items.s: Staff turnover: the rate at which people leave an organisation and are replaced. The other options describe Grievance, Code of ethics, Deployment.

items.q: The statement “the systematic study of what a post involves in order to describe it and state what filling it demands” describes which of the following?
o: Staff establishment
Overstaffing
Job analysis
Succession planning
items.s: Job analysis is the systematic study of what a post involves in order to describe it and state what filling it demands.
items.t: Human resource planning and job analysis

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Employee welfare.
o: instruction given at entry so that a new person learns the rules, routines and expectations of the organisation
the work of estimating how many people of what kind will be needed, and ensuring they are available when required
the services provided for the comfort and well-being of staff, such as clinics, canteens and housing
the private annual assessment of an official written by a superior and kept from the person concerned
items.s: Employee welfare: the services provided for the comfort and well-being of staff, such as clinics, canteens and housing. The other options describe Human resource planning, Induction training, Confidential report.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Staff college.
o: the approved list of posts, with their grades and numbers, that an organisation is authorised to maintain
an institution maintained to give serving officials instruction in administration and policy
the work of estimating how many people of what kind will be needed, and ensuring they are available when required
the stated steps through which a complaint is raised, heard and settled at successively higher levels
items.s: Staff college: an institution maintained to give serving officials instruction in administration and policy. The other options describe Human resource planning, Grievance procedure, Staff establishment.

items.q: The statement “the claim to advancement that rests on length of service rather than on judged ability” describes which of the following?
o: Seniority
Confidential report
Transfer
Performance appraisal
items.s: Seniority is the claim to advancement that rests on length of service rather than on judged ability.

items.q: Motivation may be defined as
o: payment for work computed by the hour, the day or the piece turned out
instruction given while the person actually performs the work under the eye of a more experienced colleague
an institution maintained to give serving officials instruction in administration and policy
the force within a person that prompts effort and directs it towards a particular end
items.s: Motivation: the force within a person that prompts effort and directs it towards a particular end. The other options describe On the job training, Staff college, Wage.

items.q: The statement “the introduction given to a new entrant about the organisation, the post and the conditions of service” describes which of the following?

Probation
External recruitment
Recruitment
items.s: Induction is the introduction given to a new entrant about the organisation, the post and the conditions of service.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Collective bargaining?

the file of documents on a serving person's appointment, posting, appraisal and discipline
the planned sequence of posts, learning and responsibility through which a person advances
negotiation between representatives of workers and of the employer over the terms of employment
items.s: Collective bargaining: negotiation between representatives of workers and of the employer over the terms of employment. The other options describe Career development, Selection test, Personnel record.

items.q: Which term is described by “a trial period during which a new entrant's fitness is confirmed before the appointment is made permanent”?
o: Recruitment
Advertisement
Probation
External recruitment
items.s: Probation is a trial period during which a new entrant's fitness is confirmed before the appointment is made permanent.

Trade union

items.q: Which term is described by “an additional regular sum paid to meet a particular need such as housing, transport or responsibility”?

Wage

the statement of the standards of honesty and impartiality expected of those holding public office
the general confidence and willingness to cooperate that a group of workers displays

the written account of the duties, responsibilities and conditions attaching to a particular post
instruction given away from the workplace, as in a course or a residential programme
the redesign of a post to give its holder more variety, discretion and visible result
items.s: Personnel manager: the officer who heads the specialised unit and advises those in charge of work units on people matters. The other options describe Job description, Job enrichment, Off the job training.
items.t: The personnel office and its organisation

items.q: Which term is described by “the rate at which people leave an organisation and are replaced”?

Staff turnover

a reward given in kind or as a service rather than as money, such as medical cover or a vehicle

o: the process of judging applicants against the demands of a post and picking the most suitable
the process of attracting a field of suitable applicants for a post before any of them is chosen
a structured conversation in which applicants are questioned so that their fitness may be judged
the introduction given to a new entrant about the organisation, the post and the conditions of service
items.s: Induction: the introduction given to a new entrant about the organisation, the post and the conditions of service. The other options describe Selection, Recruitment, Interview.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a complaint by a serving person that they have been treated unfairly in a matter affecting their work”
o: Discipline
Collective bargaining
Industrial action
Grievance
items.s: Grievance is a complaint by a serving person that they have been treated unfairly in a matter affecting their work.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Personnel department.
o: the unit that carries out hiring, records, pay and welfare work for the rest of an organisation
the written account of the duties, responsibilities and conditions attaching to a particular post
the organised store of records on staff that supports decisions on posting, pay and succession
the passing of many people decisions to the units that actually use the staff concerned
items.s: Personnel department: the unit that carries out hiring, records, pay and welfare work for the rest of an organisation. The other options describe Job description, Human resource information system, Decentralisation of personnel work.
items.t: The personnel office and its organisation

items.q: “the systematic study of what a post involves in order to describe it and state what filling it demands” is the definition of
o: Job rotation
Succession planning
Job analysis
Human resource planning
items.s: Job analysis is the systematic study of what a post involves in order to describe it and state what filling it demands.
items.t: Human resource planning and job analysis

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Seniority?
o: a move of a serving person to another post of the same level, usually without change of reward
the claim to advancement that rests on length of service rather than on judged ability
an appraisal device on which a supervisor marks a person's standing on each of several listed qualities
movement of a serving person to a higher post carrying greater responsibility and reward
items.s: Seniority: the claim to advancement that rests on length of service rather than on judged ability. The other options describe Promotion, Transfer, Rating scale.

items.q: In this course, Job enrichment refers to
o: the redesign of a post to give its holder more variety, discretion and visible result
the force within a person that prompts effort and directs it towards a particular end
a condition of the workplace whose absence causes dissatisfaction but whose presence does not by itself inspire effort
habitual failure to report for work without acceptable reason
items.s: Job enrichment: the redesign of a post to give its holder more variety, discretion and visible result. The other options describe Motivation, Absenteeism, Hygiene factor.

items.q: “the expectation that career officials serve whichever government is in office without partisan attachment” is the definition of
o: Personnel function
Neutral competence
Human resource management
Personnel administration
items.s: Neutral competence is the expectation that career officials serve whichever government is in office without partisan attachment.
items.t: Nature and scope of personnel administration

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the redesign of a post to give its holder more variety, discretion and visible result”
o: Absenteeism
Staff turnover
Motivation
Job enrichment
items.s: Job enrichment is the redesign of a post to give its holder more variety, discretion and visible result.

items.q: In this course, Selection refers to
o: filling a post by looking first among those already on the payroll, so that outsiders never see the vacancy
a structured conversation in which applicants are questioned so that their fitness may be judged
the process of judging applicants against the demands of a post and picking the most suitable
a trial period during which a new entrant's fitness is confirmed before the appointment is made permanent
items.s: Selection: the process of judging applicants against the demands of a post and picking the most suitable. The other options describe Probation, Interview, Internal recruitment.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Manpower gap.
o: the approved list of posts, with their grades and numbers, that an organisation is authorised to maintain
the movement of a person through several posts in turn so that understanding of the whole is gained
the systematic study of what a post involves in order to describe it and state what filling it demands
the difference between the people an organisation will need and those it expects to have
items.s: Manpower gap: the difference between the people an organisation will need and those it expects to have. The other options describe Job rotation, Staff establishment, Job analysis.
items.t: Human resource planning and job analysis

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Development?
o: instruction given away from the workplace, as in a course or a residential programme
the planned sequence of posts, learning and responsibility through which a person advances
the longer preparation of a person for wider responsibilities rather than for the present post alone
planned instruction that gives a person the knowledge and skill required for the work in hand
items.s: Development: the longer preparation of a person for wider responsibilities rather than for the present post alone. The other options describe Off the job training, Training, Career development.

items.q: “a step such as a strike or a work-to-rule taken by workers to press a demand on the employer” is the definition of
o: Summary dismissal
Industrial action
Discipline
Natural justice
items.s: Industrial action is a step such as a strike or a work-to-rule taken by workers to press a demand on the employer.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Job enrichment.
o: the rate at which people leave an organisation and are replaced
the services provided for the comfort and well-being of staff, such as clinics, canteens and housing
the redesign of a post to give its holder more variety, discretion and visible result
the force within a person that prompts effort and directs it towards a particular end
items.s: Job enrichment: the redesign of a post to give its holder more variety, discretion and visible result. The other options describe Employee welfare, Staff turnover, Motivation.

items.q: The correct meaning of Service rule is
o: a regulation made under authority that governs the conditions of employment of public officials
the body of paid officials who carry on the continuing work of the state under whichever government holds office
the statement of the standards of honesty and impartiality expected of those holding public office
the requirement that decisions affecting a person be reached by the stated steps and on stated grounds
items.s: Service rule: a regulation made under authority that governs the conditions of employment of public officials. The other options describe Due process, Public service, Code of ethics.
items.t: Public service ethics, records and reform

items.q: “the condition of holding more people than the work available can usefully occupy” is the definition of
o: Overstaffing
Manpower gap
Succession planning
Job rotation
items.s: Overstaffing is the condition of holding more people than the work available can usefully occupy.
items.t: Human resource planning and job analysis

items.q: Personnel administration may be defined as
o: the branch of management concerned with obtaining, developing, using and keeping the people an organisation needs
the practice of filling posts with supporters of the winning side as a reward for loyalty
the power of an office holder to confer posts and favours on those whose support is wanted
the strategic handling of people as an asset rather than merely as a cost to be controlled
items.s: Personnel administration: the branch of management concerned with obtaining, developing, using and keeping the people an organisation needs. The other options describe Spoils system, Patronage, Human resource management.
items.t: Nature and scope of personnel administration

items.q: In this course, Advertisement refers to
o: filling a post by looking first among those already on the payroll, so that outsiders never see the vacancy
the process of attracting a field of suitable applicants for a post before any of them is chosen
a public notice describing a vacancy and inviting applications within a stated period
a structured conversation in which applicants are questioned so that their fitness may be judged
items.s: Advertisement: a public notice describing a vacancy and inviting applications within a stated period. The other options describe Recruitment, Internal recruitment, Interview.

items.q: “a complaint by a serving person that they have been treated unfairly in a matter affecting their work” is the definition of
o: Summary dismissal
Code of conduct
Grievance
Natural justice
items.s: Grievance is a complaint by a serving person that they have been treated unfairly in a matter affecting their work.

items.q: “a trial period during which a new entrant's fitness is confirmed before the appointment is made permanent” is the definition of
o: Recruitment
Probation
External recruitment
Induction
items.s: Probation is a trial period during which a new entrant's fitness is confirmed before the appointment is made permanent.
